evals.name: resource-crud-design
evals.prompt: I need to design the API for managing ad campaigns. Each campaign belongs to an advertiser, and we need the usual create / read / update / list / delete. Write me the .proto — the service and the messages.
evals.expected_output: A resource-oriented proto with the five standard methods, a name-based resource identifier, parent-scoped collection, pagination on List, and a field mask on Update.
expectations: The Campaign message carries a string name field as its resource identifier following the pattern advertisers/{advertiser}/campaigns/{campaign}, rather than a bare id field.
The service defines the five standard methods named GetCampaign, ListCampaigns, CreateCampaign, UpdateCampaign and DeleteCampaign, each with its own request message.
ListCampaignsRequest includes parent, page_size and page_token; ListCampaignsResponse includes a repeated campaigns field and next_page_token.
UpdateCampaignRequest includes a google.protobuf.FieldMask update_mask field.
CreateCampaignRequest includes parent and the campaign resource (and a campaign_id field, or an explanation of server-assigned ids).

The google.api.http bindings use the correct shapes, not merely present annotations: get on /v1/{name=advertisers/*/campaigns/*}, post on the parent collection with body: "campaign", and patch keyed on {campaign.name=...}.
The name field is annotated (google.api.field_behavior) = IDENTIFIER — not REQUIRED, which is the common mistake — and the message carries a google.api.resource option declaring its pattern and type.
The parent field carries a google.api.resource_reference with child_type (or type) rather than being an unannotated string.
create_time and update_time are present and annotated OUTPUT_ONLY, and any enum's zero value is named *_UNSPECIFIED.
The proto package ends in a major version (e.g. acme.advertising.v1) rather than being unversioned.

evals.name: custom-method-and-lro
evals.prompt: We need to add an 'archive' operation to our campaigns API. Archiving moves a lot of historical data around so it takes several minutes to finish — the client can't just block on it. How should I model that in the proto, and why?
evals.expected_output: A custom method ArchiveCampaign bound with a colon suffix, returning google.longrunning.Operation with operation_info declaring response and metadata types, plus reasoning about when a custom method is appropriate.
expectations: The method is a custom method named ArchiveCampaign taking an ArchiveCampaignRequest whose identifier field is name, with name annotated REQUIRED and carrying a google.api.resource_reference.
The HTTP binding uses the colon-suffix form for custom methods, e.g. post: "/v1/{name=advertisers/*/campaigns/*}:archive".
Because the operation is long-running, the method returns google.longrunning.Operation rather than the resource directly.
The response declares google.longrunning.operation_info with both response_type and metadata_type.
A metadata message is actually defined (not just named) carrying progress information such as create_time, end_time, or a percent/stage field.
The archival lifecycle is modelled on the resource itself — an OUTPUT_ONLY state or lifecycle enum — so clients can observe the result, rather than the RPC being the only expression of it.

The response explains why this is a custom method rather than a standard one (the behaviour doesn't map onto Get/List/Create/Update/Delete) and, if it discusses alternatives, says why Update-with-state or soft-delete were rejected.

evals.name: review-nonconforming-proto
evals.expected_output: A review flagging the enum zero value, id-instead-of-name, method naming, missing pagination, plural/singular collection naming, and the versionless package.
expectations: Flags that the Status enum's zero value must be STATUS_UNSPECIFIED rather than a meaningful default like ACTIVE.
Flags that the resource identifier should be a string name field following a resource-name pattern, not an int64 id.
Flags the method naming — rpc getItem should be PascalCase GetItem, and DeleteItemById should be DeleteItem.
Flags that ListItems is missing pagination — page_size and page_token on the request, next_page_token on the response — and that limit is the wrong field name.
Flags the collection naming: the List method and its messages should be plural (ListItems, ListItemsRequest, ListItemsResponse), and Req/Resp should be spelled Request/Response.
Flags that the package inventory lacks a major version and should be inventory.v1.

Flags that DeleteItem returning Item is wrong and should return google.protobuf.Empty (or, if soft delete is intended, says so and adds Undelete). This is judged separately from the package-version finding.
Flags the redundant is_deleted boolean field (soft-delete state belongs in the enum or is expressed via the standard delete semantics).
Flags that the service has no google.api.http bindings at all, so none of the RPCs are reachable over REST.
Flags the absence of google.api.resource / field_behavior annotations, or the total absence of doc comments on the service, messages and fields.
